The question about whether nuchal translucency thickness in the first trimester predicts gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) onset during pregnancy is answered by stating that NT thickness does not show a significant increase in those women who subsequently develop GDM. Therefore, NT assessment does not prove to be an useful ultrasound parameter for predicting GDM onset during pregnancy.

In other words, while nuchal translucency thickness is an important marker for potential congenital anomalies and pregnancy complications, it does not serve as a reliable predictor of the development of gestational diabetes mellitus in women undergoing routine prenatal care.
